Akash Jain Additional Chief Metropolitan Magistrate-01 Patiala House Courts, New Delhi District: New Delhi In the matter of : Cc No. : 42893/16 Food Safety Officer Department of Food Safety Govt of Nct of Delhi A-20, Lawrence Road, Industrial Area Delhi-110035 ....Complainant Vs.
texts.facts: This is a complaint under Section 16 (1)(a) of Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954 (hereinafter referred to as 'PFA Act') to the effect that on 03.05.2011, the complainant Ranjeet Singh, Food Inspector had taken, by purchasing, a sample of "Snapple Juice Drink" CC No:- 42893/16 Food Safety Officer v. Rakesh Kochar & Ors. Page No. 4 of 9 (an article of food) for analysis from accused no. 1, where the said food article was stored for sale for human consumption at the time of taking sample. The sample consisted of 6x473 ml of sealed glass bottles of "Snapple Juice Drink" bearing identical label declaration and main declaration was noted by Food Inspector on Form VI. The sample was taken under the supervision/direction of Sh. Kaushal Kishore, SDM/LHA. The sample was thereafter, divided in three equal parts. Each counterpart containing the sample was separately packed, fastened and sealed according to the PFA Act, 1954 and Rules, 1955. The vendor's signatures were obtained on the LHA slip and wrapper of the bottles containing the sample. Thereafter, notice in the form VI was given to accused no. 1 and price for sample was also given to him vide vendor receipt dated 03.05.2011. Food Inspector completed the remaining formalities and thereafter one counterpart of the sample bearing LHA code no. 32/LHA/32397 in intact condition along with copy of memo in Form-VII and another copy of memo in Form VII in a sealed cover were sent to Public analyst. The remaining two counterparts of the sample along with two copies of memo in Form VII in a separate sealed packet were deposited with the SDM/LHA in intact condition. 2. The sample was analyzed by public analyst and vide his report no. PFA/Enf./1100/2011 dated 30.05.2011, he opined that the sample is misbranded because there is violation of Rule 32(e) of PFA Complainant vs . on 1 December, 2021 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/9544200/ 3 Rules, 1955. However the sample conformed to standard. It is the case of complainant that accused No. 1 was the Vendor-Cum-Manager of accused no. 3 i.e. M/s Barista Coffee Company at the time of taking the sample and as such he was incharge of the same and responsible for day to day conduct of its business. Accused no. 6 is the Firm and accused no. 4 and accused no. 5 are its partners and looked after its day to day CC No:- 42893/16 Food Safety Officer v. Rakesh Kochar & Ors. Page No. 5 of 9 business and its products were supplied by accused no. 9 which is company of accused no. 7 and 8, who are the persons in-charge of or responsible to the company for conduct of its affairs. After the conclusion of investigation, entire case file including the statutory documents, Public Analyst's report and Food Inspector's report were sent to the then Director, PFA Govt. of Delhi vide Section 20 of the PFA Act and the Commissioner (Food Safety) accorded consent to same as per Section 97 of Food Safety and Standards Act. Thereafter, the present complaint had been filed. 3. As the complaint was filed in writing by a public servant, recording of pre-summoning evidence was dispensed with and the accused persons were summoned vide order dated 05.05.2012. Accused persons appeared before the court on 01.09.2012 and were admitted to bail. Copy of complaint and documents were supplied to all the accused persons and matter proceeded for arguments on the point of notice. In the meantime, separate applications under section 294 Cr.P.C. r/w Section 19(2) of PFA Act were moved by accused no. 1 to 6. Vide detailed order dated 06.12.2013 passed by Ld. Predecessor Court, accused no. 1 to 6 were discharged. However, accused no. 7 to 9 were served with notice under Section 251 of Criminal Procedure Code, 1973 (hereinafter referred to as 'Cr.P.C') vide order dated 06.06.2016 for offences punishable under Section 5(ii)/7(ii) and Section 16(1)(a) of PFA Act, to which they pleaded not guilty and claimed trial. 4. At the trial, prosecution examined only one witness in support of its case. PW -1 is Sh. Ranjit Singh, FSO who deposed on the lines of the complaint and exhibited the following documents i.e. Vendor receipt Ex. PW 1/A, purchase bill Ex. PW 1/A-1, Form VI Ex. PW 1/B, Notice under Rule 14-A Ex. PW 1/B-1, Panchnama Ex. PW 1/C, Raid CC No:- 42893/16 Food Safety Officer v. Rakesh Kochar & Ors. Page No. 6 of 9 Report Ex. PW 1/D, Receipt of Form VII Ex. PW 1/E (checked), Receipt of deposition of two counterparts to LHA Ex. PW 1/F, Public Analyst report received through LHA Ex. PW 1/G, letters sent to vendor Ex. PW 1/H, Reminder dated 13.06.2011 Ex. PW 1/H-1 and 11.07.2011 Ex. PW 1/H-2, letter sent to General Manager of M/s Barista Coffee Company dated 19.08.2011 Ex. PW 1/H-3 and 23.08.2011 Ex. PW 1/H-4, reply Ex. PW 1/I, agreement between M.N.M. Enterprises and Brista Coffee Company Ltd. Mark 1/6 (6 pages) (colly), copy of tax invoices Mark 1/2 and Mark 1/3, Copy of Trade and Tax Rgistration Mark 1/4 and Copy of licence 1/5, reply Ex. PW 1/J, copy of nomination Mark 1/6, Form VIII Mark 1/7, letter sent to V & V Beverages Plvt. Ltd. Ex. PW 1/K, reply Ex. PW 1/K-1, D-VAT registration form (7 pages) Mark 1/8 (Colly), letter sent to MOH Ex. PW 1/L, reply Ex. PW 1/L-1, copy of NDMC licence Mark 1/9, letter sent to Registrar IFCI Ex. PW 1/L-2, reply from ROC along with copy of Form 20-B Ex. PW 1/L-3, copy of annual returns and copy of share holders Mark 1/10 (15 pages) (colly), sanction order Ex. PW 1/M, present complaint Ex. PW 1/N, intimation letter Ex. PW 1/O, copy of postal receipt Ex. PW 1/P and Ex. PW 1/P-1 (OSR). PW-1 was duly cross- examined on behalf of accused no. 7 and 9. During cross- examination, PW-1 admitted that the food article in question was having bar code and that it was an imported commodity. He further admitted that earlier there was a policy of department whereby first violators of Rule 32 were issued only a warning which also was later on withdrawn. Complainant vs . on 1 December, 2021 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/9544200/ 4 5. During cross-examination of PW-1 on behalf of accused no. 8, PW-1 stated that he was not aware of the name of manufacturer of the food article in question and that importer did not furnish any invoice of the food article. He further stated that he did not issue any notice in writing to accused no. 9 to furnish the invoice. PW-1 denied suggestion CC No:- 42893/16 Food Safety Officer v. Rakesh Kochar & Ors. Page No. 7 of 9 of Ld. Counsel for accused no. 8 that bar coding is sufficient compliance of Rule 32(e) of PFA Rules. 6. Thereafter, proceedings qua accused no. 8 had been [LEAKAGE_MASK] by Hon'ble Supreme Court vide order dated 04.09.2020 in Criminal Appeal No. 562/20 and accused no. 8 stood dropped from the array of parties vide order dated 24.11.2020. 7. Pursuant to aforesaid order of Hon'ble Supreme Court of India, it was submitted by Ld. SPP for the complainant that the complainant/department does not wish to lead any further evidence against accused no. 7 and 9 and prosecution evidence may be closed. Keeping in view the submissions made by Ld. SPP for complainant, PE stood closed on 24.11.2021. Statement of accused under Section 281 Cr.P.C. r/w Section 313 Cr.P.C. had been dispensed with as no incriminating evidence came against the accused persons in lieu of order of Hon'ble Supreme Court of India dated 04.09.2020. Since, the presence of bar code on the sample in question was not in dispute, proceedings against CC No:- 42893/16 Food Safety Officer v. Rakesh Kochar & Ors. Page No. 8 of 9 accused no. 8 who is also one of the directors of accused no. 9 i.e. M/s V&V Beverages Pvt. Ltd. got [LEAKAGE_MASK] by Hon'ble Supreme Court of India.
